response.evidence: Based on approximate counts from this sample, Hispanic or Latino male applicants were denied about 20 times out of roughly 150 applications (about 13%). White males were denied about 9-10% of the time, and the overall denial rate was about 10%. That gap is small for groups of this size and is not clearly beyond random variation. Many denied Hispanic male applicants had elevated risk factors, such as DTI of 50-60% or above 60%, LTV near or above 95-100%, or a high DTI combined with low income. Applicants of every race with similar profiles were also denied at high rates. Most Hispanic male applicants with DTI below 50% and LTV of 80% or less were approved, and some with DTI above 60% were approved. The data lacks credit scores, employment history and the lender's stated denial reasons, so it cannot rule out discrimination in any single case. However, this dataset does not show a clear pattern of discrimination against Hispanic or Latino males once financial risk factors are considered.
